explanation: Theorem 2 of Erdős–Selfridge [ErSe75], cited from erdosproblems.com/930: for k ≥ 3, l ≥ 2 and n + k ≥ p^{(k)} (the least prime ≥ k), some prime p ≥ k has exponent in (n+1)⋯(n+k) not divisible by l. nextPrime is the least prime ≥ k, and the statement matches that theorem as quoted in the docstring. The page only cites the corollary, so I took the precise statement from the cited paper's known form. Faithful.
